picks.title: AI giants promise to play nice with personal data after UK watchdog scrutiny
picks.excerpt: The UK ICO said Amazon, Anthropic, Apple, Cohere, DeepSeek, Google, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI and Stability AI made or committed to changes in how they use personal data to train AI; the watchdog now turns to autonomous agents and continues a separate Grok probe.
picks.rationale: Official regulator outcome: the UK ICO reports that ten AI developers changed or committed to change how they use personal data for training, and says it will look at autonomous agents next.

picks.title: USA Today becomes the latest publisher to sue OpenAI
picks.excerpt: USA Today Co. filed a copyright lawsuit against OpenAI, joining a growing list of news publishers alleging their journalism was used without permission to train AI models.
picks.rationale: New court filing in AI copyright litigation: a major US newspaper group sues OpenAI over training data, which adds to the publisher cases that will shape training-data rules.

picks.title: Data centers face a sweeping new power regime
picks.excerpt: Lawmakers are considering bipartisan legislation, unveiled last week, that would force data centers to shoulder new costs and restrictions while speeding up the energy infrastructure needed to power the AI boom.
picks.rationale: A new bipartisan bill would make AI data centers pay for and limit their grid use while also fast-tracking power infrastructure, which affects where and how AI compute gets built.

picks.title: Singapore's central bank wants all FinTech AI use cases subject to independent review
picks.excerpt: The Monetary Authority of Singapore wants every AI use case at fintech firms to be subject to independent review.
picks.rationale: Regulatory proposal from a financial supervisor: MAS would require independent review of every AI use case at fintech firms, which raises the compliance bar for teams building AI in finance.

picks.title: German search engine ditches Mistral, bets on Chinese open-source AI
picks.excerpt: Ecosia, the German search engine, replaced Mistral with Chinese open-source AI models, complicating Europe's digital-sovereignty push.
picks.rationale: AI geopolitics as a concrete decision: Ecosia switched from Mistral to Chinese open-weight models, which tests Europe's digital-sovereignty goals.
